According to Certificate of Naturalization # 129572, dated July 12, 1935: Dan was single, of Romanian parents, 29 years old, and 5 foot, 5 inches tall. He was white, with dark complexion, had brown eyes, and dark brown hair. He had a scar on his left thumb.

Dan arrived in Canada under emigration authorization #6448/5977, passport 27468; (passport dated April 28, 1926), Transport Contract #1962.

He left Calinesti, Ceremus (Romania) on May 20, 1926 and sailed from the Port of Paris, France by 3rd Class. On May 29, 1926, he arrived in the Port of Quebec, and then travelled on CPR Rail Pass #4644 by 3rd Class to Winnipeg, Manitoba.

Dan's profession was listed as a laborer. The cost of the trip to Winnipeg from Europe was $462.50.

Dan resided in Elm Creek, Manitoba on April 20, 1935, and at the Nugget Hotel at 711 Main Street in Winnipeg on June 21, 1935, and at 186 Magnus Avenue on August 20, 1940. He later resided at 68 Granville Street during WW II, and finally at 925 Inkster Boulevard.

Dan Pongoski was a registered voter on August 20, 1940. On the "4 - 9" - 1943 he was listed as a restaurant cook, age 37, 175 lbs., and 5 foot 6 inches in height.

Dan became eligible for Old Age Security in May 1971.

In the later part of his illness, Dan he was a patient of the Municipal Hospitals. Dan died after a lengthy illness (stroke).

He was employed by Ray and Jerry's Restaurant, and went on to own and operate Jimmy's Restaurant in downtown Winnipeg. The restaurant was destroyed in a major fire.

Honorary pallbearers at the funeral were friends Stephen Dudrik, George Zelizey, William Krestanowich, John Danelak, William Ternowetsky and Roman Floresco.

Pallbearers were Fred Taylor and nephews Gerry Lacho, Dennis Lacho, Larry Lacko, Wayne Lacko, and Allen Ribachuk.

Certificate of Death #121852, Registration # 3444.

Cropo Funeral Home, Main Street at Luxton Avenue in Winnipeg was in care of arrangements.

Died at the age of 73 years.
